name: After § 31
title: REPORT on the situation of fundamental rights in the European Union in 2024 and 2025
part_text: 31a. Reiterates that freedom of expression constitutes one of the fundamental pillars of democratic societies and includes the right to express opinions that may be controversial or challenge prevailing views; stresses that any limitations to this freedom must be provided for by law, be strictly necessary and proportionate, and must not be used to restrict legitimate public debate on matters of general interest, including those of an ethical, moral and religious nature;
